Opacity-based Early Termination is a family of volume rendering optimizations that halt the front-to-back ray integration loop once the accumulated opacity exceeds a predefined threshold, thereby skipping samples that contribute negligibly to the final pixel color [S1].

The claim states that Opacity-based Early Termination halts ray integration when accumulated opacity exceeds a threshold. Source [S1] explicitly defines this optimization as 'terminating resampling along a ray when its accumulated opacity exceeds a user-selected threshold of opaqueness.' The additional context in the claim regarding 'skipping samples that contribute negligibly' is the inherent logical consequence of terminating the loop early in a front-to-back accumulation algorithm, which is consistent with the definition provided in the evidence.
supported
